title: Quantum Broker: QoS-Aware Distribution of Quantum Computations
authors: Giuseppe Bisicchia, Alessandro Bocci, Jose Garcia-Alonso, Juan Manuel Murillo, Antonio Brogi
abstract: Cloud-accessible quantum computing has made heterogeneous Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) available through provider platforms that differ in qubit technology, calibration state, queueing behavior, and pricing model. This heterogeneity makes execution management a quantum-engineering concern: a quantum circuit may be executable on several backends, but the resulting cost, latency, fidelity, and reproducibility depend on backend selection and on how measurement shots are allocated. This paper presents the Quantum Broker, an open-source and provider-agnostic framework for Quality-of-Service-aware quantum execution management. The framework operationalizes shot-wise distribution by exploiting the statistical independence of quantum measurement shots to dispatch a single circuit across multiple heterogeneous QPUs according to user-defined constraints and optimization objectives. It combines a modular execution architecture, interchangeable backend-profiling strategies, and the Quantum QoS Specification Language (QQSpec), a declarative language for expressing QoS requirements. Dispatch planning is supported by two solver backends: a mixed-integer linear-programming (MILP) solver, and a nonlinear dual-annealing solver. Experiments on benchmark quantum circuits and noisy simulator backends show that the Quantum Broker can produce feasible QoS-aware dispatch plans under heterogeneous backend conditions and can improve QoS satisfaction with respect to single-backend and naive multi-backend baselines. The results also expose a practical trade-off between planning time and dispatch quality, with the nonlinear solver producing higher-quality allocations at increased computational cost. Overall, the Quantum Broker provides an extensible execution-management layer for engineering portable, reproducible, and QoS-aware quantum software over fragmented quantum cloud infrastructures.
summary: This paper introduces the Quantum Broker, a framework designed to manage quantum circuit execution across diverse, cloud-based quantum hardware. It solves the complex problem of optimizing resource allocation (like shot distribution) to meet specific Quality-of-Service goals such as minimizing cost or maximizing fidelity. By providing a standardized, pluggable layer, it significantly advances the engineering maturity of quantum software development.
main_problem: Managing quantum circuit execution across heterogeneous, cloud-accessible Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) to satisfy complex Quality-of-Service (QoS) requirements in a portable and reproducible manner.
main_result: The Quantum Broker framework successfully produces feasible QoS-aware dispatch plans, improving QoS satisfaction over single-backend or naive multi-backend approaches.
method: It employs shot-wise distribution, dispatching a single circuit across multiple QPUs based on optimization plans generated by MILP or nonlinear dual-annealing solvers.
model_or_system: The system involves cloud-accessible QPUs with varying technologies and behaviors. The core model is the QoS-aware dispatch problem, managed by the open-source Quantum Broker framework.
key_observables: Cost, latency, fidelity, queueing delays, and the final measurement counts (reconstructed output distribution).
important_parameters: Shot allocation ($n_m/N$), QoS constraints (expressed via QQSpec), and the choice of optimization solver (MILP vs. nonlinear).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes statistical independence of quantum measurement shots for distribution. Current evaluations use noisy simulators and do not fully capture real-world temporal variability or provider-side constraints.
figures_summary: Not specified (The notes mention Table 1 comparing novelty against previous shot-wise work).
paper_structure: The paper details the Quantum Broker design, covering the QoS-aware dispatch problem, the shot-wise distribution methodology, and presents evaluations comparing different solver backends and aggregation policies.
why_interesting: It addresses the critical engineering challenge of making quantum algorithms portable and robust by abstracting away the hardware heterogeneity and operational constraints of cloud quantum backends.
